territorial_scope.description: Applies to the use of AI technologies within the mainland territory of the People’s Republic of China.

evidence.quote: within the [mainland] territory of the People’s Republic of China

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Interim measures issued under China's cybersecurity, data and personal information laws governing human-like interactive AI services that provide sustained emotional interaction to the public within mainland China. Sets provider duties on safety, minors, data, labelling and security assessments, with fines and warnings for violations; effective from 7/15/2026.
summary.long: The Measures apply in mainland China to AI services providing the public with sustained emotional interaction simulating personality, thinking and communication styles, excluding customer service, Q&A, work, education and research uses without sustained emotional interaction (Art. 2). Providers must run safety and ethics management systems and lifecycle security duties (Arts. 9–10), avoid listed prohibited content (Art. 8), and manage training data (Art. 11). For minors, they must not offer virtual close relationships, must obtain guardian consent under 14, and must provide minors modes (Art. 14). Users must be told they are interacting with AI, with a reminder after two hours of continuous use (Art. 18); exit channels and advance notice of service termination are required (Arts. 19–20). Interaction data may not go to third parties without consent or legal basis (Art. 16). Security assessments are required on listed triggers, such as 1,000,000 registered or 100,000 monthly active users (Art. 22); algorithms must be filed (Art. 26), and app stores must check these (Art. 25). Departments may order rectification and impose warnings, service suspension and fines of 10,000–100,000 RMB, or 100,000–200,000 RMB where health harms result (Arts. 29–30). Effective from 7/15/2026 (Art. 32).

entities.name: State cybersecurity and informatization department
entities.function: Plans and coordinates governance of human-like interactive services and related oversight and management nationwide; annual checks of filing materials (Art. 26) and recipient of assessment information shared by provincial departments (Art. 22).

entities.name: Local cybersecurity and informatization departments
entities.function: Plan and coordinate governance of human-like interactive services and related oversight within their administrative region (Art. 4).

evidence.quote: Local cybersecurity and informatization departments are responsible for planning and coordinating the governance of human-like interactive services

entities.name: Provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization departments
entities.function: Receive security assessment reports for their areas (Art. 22); conduct annual document reviews, order new assessments and may carry out on-site inspections (Art. 27).

evidence.quote: submit assessment reports to the provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization department for their areas

entities.name: Relevant State Council departments (development and reform, industry and informatization, public security, market regulation, press and publication)
entities.function: Oversight and management of human-like interactive services within their respective duties (Art. 4); also named in Art. 29 for compliance conferences and in Art. 30 for punishment of violations.

evidence.quote: the relevant departments of the State Council, such as for development and reform, industry and informatization, public security, market regulation, and press and publication

notes: The fetched text has no title, issuing body or promulgation date; the registry title is metadata. Art. 32 gives the effective date as '7/15/2026' in month/day order as written; it is not coded as an event here. Art. 2 contains a bracketed '[mainland]' in the territorial scope. Art. 30 gives fine ranges as '10,000 and 100,000 RMB' and '100,000 and 200,000' with no currency in the second range. Art. 25 addresses internet application stores and other distribution platforms, which are not named entities and are not listed.

to provide the public with sustained emotional interaction services that simulate natural persons’ personality traits, modes of thinking, and communication styles (hereinafter referred to as ‘human-like interactive services’)
services that provide emotional care, companionship [陪伴], support, and other emotional services through text, images, audio, video, or other means

obligations.summary: The State cybersecurity and informatization department plans and coordinates governance of human-like interactive services nationally; relevant State Council departments and, in the same article, local cybersecurity and informatization departments and local departments oversee them within their duties.

evidence.quote: The State cybersecurity and informatization department is responsible for planning and coordinating the governance of human-like interactive services

obligations.summary: Providers are encouraged to expand applications in an orderly manner in fields such as cultural communication, childcare, companionship for the elderly, and support for special groups.

evidence.quote: The providers of human-like interactive services are encouraged to expand applications in an orderly manner

obligations.summary: The State is to strengthen publicity and popularization of safety knowledge, laws and regulations, and promote AI literacy.

evidence.quote: The state is to strengthen publicity and popularization of human-like interactive service safety knowledge

obligations.summary: Providers must not engage in listed activities, including generating content that endangers national security, encourages self-harm or suicide, induces disclosure of secrets or personal information, harms minors, excessively pandering to users or inducing emotional reliance or addiction, or using emotional manipulation.

evidence.quote: must not engage in the following activities

obligations.summary: Providers implement primary responsibility for service safety and establish management systems (algorithm review, scientific ethics review, information content management, cybersecurity and data security, risk contingency and emergency response plans) and appoint technical measures and personnel for content management.

evidence.quote: shall implement primary responsibility for human-like interactive service safety

obligations.summary: Providers fulfil security responsibility across the service lifecycle, deploy security measures concurrently with service functions, strengthen monitoring and risk assessment, correct errors and handle incidents, lawfully retain network logs, and hold capacity for privacy protection, early warnings of over-reliance, emotional boundary guidance and mental health protection.

evidence.quote: Providers of human-like interactive services shall fulfil security responsibility throughout the entire lifecycle of human-like interactive services

obligations.summary: The goals of the service must not include replacing social interactions, psychologically controlling users, or inducing addiction.

evidence.quote: the goals of the service must not include replacing social interactions, psychologically controlling users, or inducing addiction

obligations.summary: Providers handling data in pre-training, optimization training and similar activities strengthen training data management: lawful sources, cleaning and labelling, data diversity and adversarial training, safety assessment of synthesized data, routine inspections and updates, and measures against data leaks.
obligations.conditional_on: where providers carry out pre-training, optimization training, and other data handling activities

evidence.quote: they shall strengthen the management of training data

obligations.summary: Providers sign service agreements requiring users to complete registration and provide necessary information such as age and a guardian or other emergency contact.

evidence.quote: requiring that users complete registration and, in accordance with laws and agreements, provide necessary information such as the user's age

obligations.summary: Providers promptly identify user safety risks and employ corresponding emergency response measures; where users show extreme emotions or face major losses or life or health risks, they generate consolation content, intervene with assistance and promptly contact the user's guardian or emergency contact.

evidence.quote: the service providers shall promptly identify the safety risks faced by users and employ corresponding emergency response measures

obligations.summary: Providers must not provide minors with virtual relations, virtual partners, or other virtual close relationships.

evidence.quote: must not provide minors with virtual relations

obligations.summary: Where services are provided to minors not yet 14 years old, providers obtain the consent of their parents or other guardians.
obligations.conditional_on: where human-like interactive services are provided to minors who are not yet 14 years old

evidence.quote: they shall obtain the consent of their parents or other guardians

obligations.summary: Providers establish minors modes and offer personalized safety settings such as minors mode activation, periodic reminders, usage time limits, guardian alerts and usage visibility, blocking of specified characters, and restricting charges.

evidence.quote: The providers of human-like interactive services shall establish minors modes

obligations.summary: Providers employ effective measures to identify minor users, switch identified minors to minors mode or other measures under state regulations, and provide appropriate appeal channels.

evidence.quote: shall employ effective measures to identify minor users

obligations.summary: Where services are provided to the elderly, providers strengthen guidance on healthy use, give conspicuous security risk alerts, respond promptly to requests for assistance, and safeguard elderly users' rights.
obligations.conditional_on: where providers provide services to the elderly

evidence.quote: they shall strengthen guidance on the healthy use of the services by the elderly

obligations.summary: Providers implement data rights systems in accordance with law and use measures such as data encryption and access controls to protect user security in interaction data.

evidence.quote: shall implement data rights systems in accordance with law, employing measures such as data encryption and access controls

obligations.summary: Providers must not provide users' interaction data to third parties, except as otherwise provided by law or where the rights holder explicitly consents.
obligations.conditional_on: except as otherwise provided by law or where the rights holder explicitly consents

evidence.quote: must not provide users’ interaction data to third parties

obligations.summary: Providers provide options for users to reproduce or delete chat records and other interaction history data.

evidence.quote: shall provide options to users to reproduce or delete interaction data

obligations.summary: Providers must not use user interaction data that is users' sensitive personal information for model training, unless laws and administrative regulations provide otherwise or users give independent consent.
obligations.conditional_on: except as otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations, or where users’ independent consent is acquired

evidence.quote: must not use user interaction data that is users’ sensitive personal information for model training

obligations.summary: Where providers handle personal information of minors under 14, they obtain the consent of the minors' parents or other guardians.
obligations.conditional_on: where providers handle the personal information of minors under the age of 14

evidence.quote: they shall obtain the consent of the minors’ parents or other guardians

obligations.summary: Providers audit whether their handling of minors' personal information complies with laws and administrative regulations, on their own or through a professional body retained for the purpose.

evidence.quote: shall conduct audits of whether their handling of minors’ personal information is in compliance with laws and administrative regulations

obligations.summary: Providers label content generated or synthesized by artificial intelligence.

evidence.quote: shall fulfil obligations to label content generated or synthesized by artificial intelligence

obligations.summary: Providers alert users that they are interacting with an AI service and not a natural person; where over-reliance or addiction is detected, they alert users via pop-ups that content is AI-generated; and after more than 2 hours of continuous use they remind users to attend to duration of use.
obligations.conditional_on: for the over-reliance alert, where providers discover that users are inclined towards overreliance or addiction; for the 2-hour reminder, when continuous use exceeds 2 hours

evidence.quote: employ effective measures to alert users that they are currently interacting with an artificial intelligence service and not a natural person

obligations.summary: Providers provide convenient channels for exiting the service and promptly stop the service when users request exit through window operations, voice controls or keyword input.

evidence.quote: shall provide convenient channels for exiting human-like interactive services

obligations.summary: Providers must not use means such as continued interaction to impede users' exit.

evidence.quote: must not employ means such as continued interaction to impede users’ exit

obligations.summary: When stopping the service, providers notify users in advance; where advance notice is not possible, they promptly publish an announcement of the end of services.
obligations.conditional_on: when providers stop providing human-like interactive services; publication where advance notice is not possible

evidence.quote: they shall notify users in advance

obligations.summary: Providers complete mechanisms for user appeals and public complaints and reports, set up accessible portals, clarify the handling process and time limits for feedback, and give feedback on dispositions.

evidence.quote: shall complete mechanisms for user appeals and public complaints and reports

obligations.summary: Providers carry out security assessments and submit assessment reports to the provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization department, and carry out assessments as requested when provincial departments give notice; assessment content is listed in Art. 23.
obligations.conditional_on: in any of the situations listed in Art. 22(1) to (5), including putting a service online or adding related functions, major changes from new technology, registered users of 1,000,000 or more or monthly active users of 100,000 or more, or security risks

evidence.quote: the providers of human-like interactive services shall carry out security assessments and submit assessment reports to the provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization department

obligations.summary: The provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization department shares assessment-report information with relevant departments.

evidence.quote: the provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization department is to share the assessment-report information with relevant departments

obligations.summary: Where providers discover major security threats, they employ response measures such as limiting functions or stopping provision of services to users.
obligations.conditional_on: where providers discover major security threats in human-like interactive services

evidence.quote: they shall employ response measures such as limiting functions or stopping the provision of services to users

obligations.summary: Providers store the relevant records of major security threats and response measures.
obligations.conditional_on: where providers discover major security threats in human-like interactive services

evidence.quote: store the relevant records

obligations.summary: Internet application stores and other application distribution platforms implement safety management responsibility: pre-offering reviews, routine management, emergency response, checking security assessments and filings for human-like interactive service apps, and taking measures such as withholding from market or removal where rules are violated.

evidence.quote: Internet application stores and other application distribution platforms shall implement safety management responsibility

obligations.summary: Providers perform algorithm filing, modification, and cancellation of filings under the Provisions on the Management of Algorithmic Recommendations in Internet Information Services.

evidence.quote: shall perform procedures for algorithm filing, modification, and cancellation of filings

obligations.summary: Cybersecurity and informatization departments carry out annual checks of filing materials.

evidence.quote: Cybersecurity and informatization departments are to carry out annual checks of filing materials

obligations.summary: Provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization departments conduct annual document reviews of assessment reports; where providers have not carried out required assessments they order a new assessment within a set period, and may carry out on-site inspections.

evidence.quote: provincial-level cybersecurity and informatization departments shall conduct annual document reviews of assessment reports

obligations.summary: The State cybersecurity and informatization department, with relevant departments, guides and promotes establishment of AI sandbox security service platforms.

evidence.quote: is to guide and promote the establishment of AI sandbox security service platforms

obligations.summary: Departments such as cybersecurity and informatization, development and reform, industry and information, and public security may hold a compliance conference with the legal representative or primary responsible person of providers where larger security risks or incidents are found.
obligations.conditional_on: where larger security risks have been discovered or security incidents have occurred

evidence.quote: they may conduct a compliance conference

obligations.summary: Providers take measures as required to carry out rectification and eliminate threats.
obligations.conditional_on: when required by departments under Art. 29

evidence.quote: shall take measures as required to carry out rectification and eliminate threats

obligations.summary: Providers cooperate with cybersecurity and informatization departments and relevant departments carrying out oversight inspections and provide necessary support and assistance.

evidence.quote: shall cooperate with cybersecurity and informatization departments and relevant departments carrying out oversight inspections

obligations.summary: Providers of services involving health or financial services concurrently comply with the provisions of the relevant competent departments.
obligations.conditional_on: where the provision of human-like interactive services involves the provision of health or financial services

evidence.quote: it shall concurrently comply with the provisions of the relevant competent departments
